# Core source-release completion and recovery

npm publication uses the existing manual `core-stage.yml`, restricted `core-stage-review` environment, trusted publisher, provenance, and separate npm owner approval. `tag-release.yml` completes a GitHub source release only after that package is published. It has no `npm publish`, `npm stage publish`, or `id-token` permission. Ordinary PR acceptance follows the one required `verify` check and zero required human reviews; no extra review or environment-readiness sentinel gates this completion workflow.

Create a new protected version tag only at its eligible accepted main commit, after verifying the staged package. The completion workflow checks private source identity against package/source/lock metadata, protected remote tag identity, main first-parent history and current remote main visibility. It builds the exact isolated public-form archive, verifies registry identity, SHA-512 and bytes, and cryptographically checks npm signatures and SLSA provenance for that archive, repository, source commit, `core-stage.yml`, `refs/heads/main`, and `workflow_dispatch`. It rechecks remote tag identity and definite GitHub Release absence immediately before creating the release with the verified tarball and `SHA256SUMS`.

A failed completion never requires republishing npm. If npm publication succeeded but GitHub completion failed before creating a release, fix the demonstrated failure and rerun the completion job against the unchanged protected tag. Existing or uncertain GitHub Release state fails closed. If a release already exists, inspect its exact target and downloaded assets; do not overwrite it automatically. Never move tags, republish versions, weaken provenance checks, or bypass protected controls. A byte, identity, or signature mismatch requires investigation.

For read-only investigation, reproduce the public-form archive from the exact accepted tag; use `RELEASE_TAG=v<version> node scripts/tag-release-cli.mjs verify-registry /absolute/path/package.tgz`. In a disposable consumer install the exact registry package with `--ignore-scripts`, then use npm 11.15.0 `audit signatures --json --include-attestations` and the resulting successful audit with `RELEASE_TAG=v<version> GITHUB_SHA=<accepted-sha> node scripts/tag-release-cli.mjs verify-stage-provenance audit.json /absolute/path/package.tgz`. The existing legacy published-provenance rehearsal remains a fixed historical check of 2.2.3 and is not the next-release source authority.
